generations.prompt:
Use case: product-mockup.
Create a NEW close-up reference sheet showing ONLY TWO tiny parts from the supplied lantern reference: S13 UPPER SEATING RING and S14 UPPER RECEIVING CAP. The whole lantern is an appearance reference, not something to reproduce on this page.
This sheet is deliberately simple so the SAME two solids can be read consistently from several directions before rapid 3D fabrication.
Layout: two spacious rows; row one S13, row two S14. Each row has four large pictures of its one unchanged object: FRONT PROFILE, RIGHT SIDE PROFILE, DIRECT TOP, THREE-QUARTER. Front and right-side are orthographic eye-level views, top is directly above, last is oblique. Both components are rotationally symmetric about the vertical axis, so FRONT and SIDE profiles MUST be IDENTICAL in outer width, total height and tier shapes. Changing view must never change the component. No additional assembled views, no exploded duplicate components, no arrows or dimension annotations.

S13: a small broad THIN bronze annular seating ring, open circular hole, rounded/chamfered edges. Low height relative to its diameter. Front/side look like the same short flat band; the top picture shows the circular hole. Never a tall narrow tube.
S14: a small bronze receiving cap immediately ABOVE S13 in the source lantern, a broad flared lower skirt tapering into a short narrow central neck. This cap has an open round socket at its top for the separate finial stem. The cap DOES NOT INCLUDE the finial ball or stem. Identical stepped silhouette in front and side. The direct top view exposes the central socket and concentric skirt.
Weathered warm bronze, subtle darkened edges and small scratches, matching the reference. Sharp clean silhouette and clear joining surfaces; restrained material detail must not distort geometry. Matte neutral light gray background, soft studio light. Large ID labels S13 and S14 and the four view labels only. Preserve realism and actual volume; not low-poly icons, no part made by printing a picture on a flat surface. The illustrated shapes are design proposals to inspect, not precise metrology or a guaranteed CAD export.
